**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: A single elongated sugarcane leaf laid flat
- **Key features**:
  - A prominent, broad **white/cream-colored stripe** running along the central midrib of the leaf
  - The surrounding leaf blade tissue remains **green** on both sides
  - A few small **reddish/orange spots** are visible within the white stripe area
  - No widespread yellowing, no typical brown circular spots, no grassy proliferation

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Brown_Spot**: Typically produces discrete oval/circular brown lesions with yellow halos scattered across the leaf blade — not matching; the image lacks those distinct spot patterns.
- **Grassy_Shoot**: A phytoplasma disease causing excessive tillering and pale thin shoots across the whole plant — not matching; this is a single leaf showing a stripe symptom.
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus causes yellowing of the midrib (especially the abaxial/lower surface) and general leaf yellowing — the stripe here is more white/cream, not the characteristic yellow midrib discoloration.
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: A fungal disease (*Fusarium sacchari*) causing chlorotic (white/pale) streaks and patches on young sugarcane leaves, running parallel to the veins, often with developing reddish-brown necrotic spots at the margins of lesions. This matches the prominent pale-white midrib stripe + reddish spots seen in the image — consistent with the chlorotic stripe phase of Pokkah Boeng.
